widget.instructions: The arrows are the two moves along the x-axis.

args.text: Compare your answer with where the second arrow ends, measured from the start of the first.

stem: A particle moves along the x-axis from x = {{x1}} m to x = {{x2}} m, then to x = {{x3}} m.
What is its displacement? Give a negative value if it points towards −x.

hints.text: Only the first and last positions matter for displacement.
Displacement = x_final − x_initial; keep the sign.
Subtract the starting position from the final position.

path-length-for-displacement.text: That is the path length. Displacement is final minus initial position.

displacement-sign.text: The size is right, but the particle ends at a smaller x than it started, so the displacement is negative.

last-leg-only.text: Displacement covers the whole journey: from the very first position to the last.

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a length.

generic.text: Final position minus initial position, with its sign.

workedSolution.text: Δx = {{x3}} − ({{x1}}) = {{ans}} m: negative, so towards −x (path length {{path}} m).

path-length-for-displacement.front: Is displacement the total distance travelled?
path-length-for-displacement.back: No. Displacement is the change in position (final − initial), with a direction; path length is the total distance covered.

displacement-sign.back: Yes. Its sign gives its direction along the axis: negative means towards −x.

last-leg-only.back: Final position minus initial position, not just the last stage.

generic.back: Δx = x_final − x_initial; the sign gives the direction.

accessibility.altText: Two arrows along the x-axis: a move to the right, then a longer move to the left.
